THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, PRAYING TO THE JUDGMENT AND AWARDED DATED 12TH DAY OF APRIL 2017 PASSED BY II ADDL.

SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT AT KALABURAGI IN MVC.No.856/2011 MAY KINDLY BE MODIFIED AND THE TOP NOTED APPEAL MAY KINDLY BE ALLOWED AND AWARD THE COMPENSATION AS PRAYED IN THE CLAIM PETITION IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING ON I.A., THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Challenging judgment and award dated 12.04.2017 passed by II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi (for short 'tribunal') in MVC no.856/2011, this appeal is filed.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Shri B.M.Kinikeri, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

It was submitted that since insurer had preferred appeal against impugned award, finding of tribunal regarding occurrence of accident, involving insured vehicle due to rash and negligent, claimant sustained injuries and liability of insurer to pay compensation are not in dispute. It was submitted as on dated of accident i.e. 14.10.2010, claimant was a 28 year NC:
2023:KHC-K:7469 old, milk vendor, who sustained several fractures which resulted in disability.
However, tribunal did not award any compensation towards 'future loss of income'.
It was submitted that claimant had filed application for leading additional evidence by way of producing documents namely, disability certificates and x-ray reports under Order 41 Rule 27 of CPC.

In view of above,
learned counsel sought for allowing appeal by passing appropriate award.

3. On other hand, Sri Shivanand Patil, learned counsel for respondent no.2-insurer would submit that since I.A. for additional evidence was filed, matter would require remand for purpose of recording evidence for marking additional documents.

4. Heard learned counsel and perused impugned judgment and award and application.
5.

Since one of main grounds for preferring appeal is about not awarding any compensation towards 'future loss of income' and as application for leading evidence in this NC: 2023:KHC-K:7469 regard Shivaraj vs Rahmathulla Khan And Anr on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194770770/
2 filed, as submitted by learned counsel for respondent no.2-insurer, matter would require remand.

entities.text: 2023:KHC-K:7469 regard Shivaraj vs Rahmathulla Khan And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Consequently, following:
ORDER Appeal is allowed.
Impugned judgment and award dated 12.04.2017 passed by tribunal is set aside.
Matter is remitted back to tribunal for fresh consideration in light of additional evidence.

In case,
claimant led further evidence, tribunal shall consider same and pass appropriate order in accordance with law.
Since claimant and insurer are represented, they are directed to appear before tribunal on 30.09.2023 without waiting fresh notice.

Tribunal shall afford adequate opportunity to parties to lead evidence as early as possible NC:
2023:KHC-K:7469 for dispose of claim petition afresh within an outer-limit of six months.
Registry to return original documents to appellant by replacing them with photo-stat copies.

Sd/-
